textPlacement.assessment: Both contexts preserve gestures and small turns as connection, alongside respectful touch and gentle adult help when necessary care must happen.
The picture list and example day remain shared, flexible supports rather than an independent task or a fixed schedule at either age.
Both contexts start with familiar family pleasures and preserve culturally personal, inexpensive rituals without pressure to create elaborate occasions.
The age variants preserve a tentative interpretation of throwing and a calm limit without treating that behavior as evidence of sufficient intake.
Both ages retain changing help needs, small attempts and the adult’s time boundary without making yesterday’s independence compulsory today.
Supported participation remains sufficient, and the separate table setup keeps its jug-carrying and repetition conditions without becoming required equipment.
The contexts preserve supported participation and the child’s appetite, with family feasibility and consultation for food concerns clearly retained.
The earlier age variants remain distinct and the older context still invites a supported turn, without expecting independent blowing, brushing or completion.
Both contexts keep the change a family consideration with extra support and tentative observation, without imposing a new age deadline.
The age variants preserve family choice, needed support and specialist help without turning particular settling or feeding examples into a general recipe.
The contexts retain brushing as necessary care with a child’s turn and gentle adult finishing, rather than equating participation with independent dental care.
Both contexts make possible readiness signs and no forcing explicit, preserving medical qualification and avoiding an expectation tied to the browse age.
The older context leaves preparation, optional choices and developing time understanding intact while preserving gentle help when leaving is necessary.
